children: Kansas City Federal Reserve President Jeff Schmid said on Friday he supported the central bank's decision this week to raise interest rates as a step towards lowering inflation that is trending above the Fed's 2% target and is not just driven by high energy costs.

"Our inflation problem is not just about energy," Schmid said in remarks prepared for delivery to a Colorado banking group, "Inflation excluding energy has also been running hot and a broad range of goods and services are showing price growth inconsistent with our price stability target."
Schmid said inflation appears to be trending above 3%.
Schmid, who is not a voter on interest rates this year, did not indicate if he felt further hikes will be needed to return inflation to the Fed's target.
